passage.title: Jack and the Beanstalk: the teacher's retelling (version 2)
paras: Jack and his mother were poor. Their only cow, Milky-White, gave no more milk, so Jack's mother sent him to market to sell her.
On the way, Jack met an old man who offered five magic beans for the cow. Jack swapped. When he got home, his mother was cross and threw the beans out of the window.
In the morning, a giant beanstalk reached up into the clouds. Jack climbed it and found a castle. Inside lived a giant with a hen that laid golden eggs.

Jack took the hen and climbed down. The giant chased him, so Jack chopped the beanstalk down. But Jack felt bad about taking what was not his. When the giant had calmed down, Jack climbed a ladder to the castle gate and gave the hen back. The giant was so surprised by Jack's honesty that he gave Jack one golden egg as a gift.
Jack and his mother sold the egg and bought a new cow. They were never poor again.

timeline.text: Jack swaps the cow for magic beans.
His mother throws the beans out of the window.
A huge beanstalk grows up to the sky.
Jack climbs it and finds a giant's castle.
Jack escapes and chops the beanstalk down.

panels.title: Is it right to take?
points: In one version Jack takes things that are not his
How could Jack solve his problem honestly?

questions.q: Put in order: Jack climbs / beans thrown out / swaps the cow
questions.a: swaps the cow, beans thrown out, Jack climbs
For example: in version 2 Jack gives back what he took

questions.q: Core: fill the comparison grid with two same and two different things
Extend: which version do you prefer? Write why with because
questions.a: For example: I prefer version 2 because Jack is honest.

questions.q: Stretch: what could be at the top of a different beanstalk?
questions.a: For example: a garden of giant flowers

questions.q: What is the SAME in both versions?
questions.a: B) A huge beanstalk grows. The beanstalk grows in both. Keeping the gold and the friendly giant only happen in one version.
